newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end sharply lower in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end sharply lower in moderate trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended sharply lower Monday in moderate trade, closing down 3.46 percent on sales of telecom and power stocks, brokers said.

The Bovespa index of the 47 most active shares fell 455 points to 12,698 points at the close. Market turnover was 930.8 million reais ($869.9 million)). Financial volume for the Bovespa index portfolio was 433.1 million reais ($404.8 million).
Brokers said continued nervousness related to the recent currency devaluations in Southeast Asia prompted a lot of investors to take profits after the bolsa's recent bull run.

"The drop is largely related to the foreign exchange instability in Asia," a broker said. "The market has also been following Wall Street which fell 60 points during today's session, but then recovered again," a broker said.
The Bovespa index plunged more than five percent in afternoon trade before picking up again toward the close of the session.
He said Wall Street's recovery could spark a slightly stronger opening on the Sao Paulo stock exchange Tuesday, but much depended on tomorrow's news.
Other traders, who had expected the bolsa to resume its upward trend today on bargain-hunting, now believe the profit-taking wave could last for another two days.
Blue-chips posted sharp losses across the board, with mining giant Cia Vale do Rio Doce prefered posting the largest drop, falling 5.24 percent to 27.10 reais.
Federal power holding Eletrobras prefered closed down 4.84 percent at 708 reais.
Telebras prefered, which accounted for 47 percent of today's trade, closed down 4.3 percent at 158 reais and state oil firm Petrobras prefered fell 3.47 percent to 306 reais.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
